title: The successive coefficient sequence stays exact on flat-term sheaf complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe, $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,B)$ such that multiplication by $t$ on $B$ is injective. Let $n>1$ and put $R_j=B/t^jB$ with projections $\pi_j:B\to R_j$ [def-pe-principal-power-ring-quotients]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There are canonical quotient ring maps $q_-:R_n\to R_{n-1}$ and $q_1:R_n\to R_1$ with $q_-\pi_n=\pi_{n-1}$ and $q_1\pi_n=\pi_1$. The local formulas
$$a(\pi_{n-1}(c))=\pi_n(tc),\qquad b(\pi_n(c))=\pi_1(c)$$
define morphisms for which
$$0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{q_-}R_{n-1}\xrightarrow{a}R_n\xrightarrow{b}\operatorname{Res}_{q_1}R_1\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_n)$ and remains short exact after restriction to $B$.
For every unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $B$-modules whose terms are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $C_j^i=R_j\otimes_B P^i$ with differential $1\otimes d_P^i$ and $R_j$ acting on the first factor. Tensoring $a,b$ with $1_P$ gives well-defined $R_n$-linear cochain maps
$$\alpha:\operatorname{Res}_{q_-}C_{n-1}\longrightarrow C_n,\qquad \beta:C_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{q_1}C_1,$$
characterized on local pure tensors by
$$\alpha(\pi_{n-1}(c)\otimes p)=\pi_n(tc)\otimes p,\qquad \beta(\pi_n(c)\otimes p)=\pi_1(c)\otimes p.$$
They form a degreewise short exact sequence of $R_n$-complexes, also degreewise short exact after restriction to $B$. These assertions do not require points of the site, sectionwise flatness of $P^i(U)$, K-flatness of $P$, or any bound on its degrees.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient exact sequence before derived tensor; agent refinement to arbitrary small ringed sites and flat-term complexes. Stacks Tags 03DA (sites-modules-lemma-abelian), 03EK (sites-modules-section-tensor-product), 03ER (sites-modules-definition-flat, item (3)).

proof.text: Write $Q_j(U)=B(U)/(t_U^j)$ for the quotient presheaves in [def-pe-principal-power-ring-quotients]. The inclusions $(t_U^n)\subseteq(t_U^{n-1})$ and $(t_U^n)\subseteq(t_U)$ give compatible quotient ring maps $Q_n\to Q_{n-1}$ and $Q_n\to Q_1$. Sheafifying these ring maps gives $q_-,q_1$ by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Their composites with $\pi_n$ are $\pi_{n-1},\pi_1$, since these equations hold before sheafification.

source.place: Second paragraph: the quotient maps in the coefficient sequence; expanded using the quotient-presheaf definition.

proof.text: For $A=B(U)$ and $x=t_U$, define $a_0:A/(x^{n-1})\to A/(x^n)$ by $[c]\mapsto[xc]$, and $b_0:A/(x^n)\to A/(x)$ by $[c]\mapsto[c]$. Changing $c$ by $x^{n-1}d$ changes $xc$ by $x^nd$, so $a_0$ is well-defined. Both maps are additive. With $A/(x^n)$ acting on the outer terms through its quotient maps, $a_0([r][c])=[xrc]=[r]a_0([c])$ and $b_0([r][c])=[r]b_0([c])$. These formulas commute with every restriction because $t$ is a global section. Thus they give morphisms of $Q_n$-module presheaves, also morphisms of $B$-module presheaves, with precisely the scalar restrictions of [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Second paragraph: multiplication by the uniformizer and the quotient map; explicit presheaf formulas and linearity.

proof.text: Multiplication by $t$ has zero kernel as a morphism of $B$-module sheaves. Since kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], multiplication by $x=t_U$ on $A=B(U)$ is injective. If $a_0([c])=0$, then $xc=x^nd=x(x^{n-1}d)$ for some $d$, and cancellation gives $c=x^{n-1}d$; hence $a_0$ is injective. The map $b_0$ is surjective, and $b_0([c])=0$ exactly when $c=xd$, in which case $[c]=a_0([d])$. Also $b_0a_0=0$. This proves the short exact sequence at every $U$. It is short exact as a sequence of $B$-module presheaves: the sectionwise kernel and cokernel factorizations commute with restrictions by their uniqueness.

source.place: Second paragraph: exactness of the coefficient sequence, with regularity and cancellation made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with coefficient presheaf $Q_n$ to the three module presheaves $Q_{n-1},Q_n,Q_1$ and the two morphisms of Step 2. It gives $R_n=Q_n^\#$-module sheaves and $R_n$-linear sheafified morphisms. To identify the outer modules, the ring-sheafification units $Q_j\to R_j$ are $Q_n$-linear for the actions induced by $q_-,q_1$. The interface therefore gives $R_n$-linear comparison maps from the module sheafifications to those restricted $R_j$. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], both ring sheafification and abelian-group sheafification have the same underlying set sheafification, with the same unit. The comparison maps are consequently inverse on underlying sets by uniqueness of sheafification, hence are module isomorphisms. The same argument with coefficient presheaf $B$ identifies their underlying $B$-modules with the $B$-module sheafifications of $Q_j$. These identifications preserve the units and both maps, so their formulas are exactly the displayed $a,b$.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); underlying sets: sites.tex Tag 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), assertions (gamma) and (epsilon).

proof.text: Sheafify the short exact sequence of $B$-module presheaves from Step 3. The functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], applicable because $B$ is a ring sheaf on the given small site. The identifications of Step 4 give the sequence $0\to R_{n-1}\xrightarrow{a}R_n\xrightarrow{b}R_1\to0$ as a short exact sequence of $B$-module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), applied with coefficient presheaf the sheaf B.

proof.text: For any ring-sheaf map on this site, restricting scalars changes only the action [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The sectionwise kernel and the sheafified sectionwise cokernel from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have unchanged underlying abelian sheaves: module sheafification has underlying abelian sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Consequently kernels, cokernels, and the image (kernel of the cokernel) have identical underlying abelian sheaves before and after restriction. Restriction therefore preserves and reflects short exactness. Apply this observation to $B\to R_n$ and the $R_n$-linear sequence of Step 4. Step 5 proves its restricted sequence short exact, so the sequence itself is short exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_n)$.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), kernel/cokernel descriptions immediately preceding it, and restriction functor immediately after Tag 03EI.

proof.text: Fix a degree $i$. The presheaf $U\mapsto R_j(U)\otimes_{B(U)}P^i(U)$ has the $R_j(U)$-action $r(s\otimes p)=(rs)\otimes p$. Its restriction maps preserve this action. Its sheafification is $C_j^i$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] extends this action to an $R_j$-module sheaf action. The maps $a\otimes1$ and $b\otimes1$ are balanced over $B$, because $a,b$ are $B$-linear. They are $R_n$-linear with the restricted outer actions: on generators, $(a\otimes1)(q_-(r)s\otimes p)=r\,a(s)\otimes p$ and $(b\otimes1)(rs\otimes p)=q_1(r)b(s)\otimes p$. The interface sheafifies these linear maps. Substituting $s=\pi_{n-1}(c)$ or $s=\pi_n(c)$ gives the asserted formulas for $\alpha^i,\beta^i$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor and associated sheaf; Tag 03CY for extending the first-factor actions.

proof.text: Define $d_j^i=1\otimes d_P^i$. It is $R_j$-linear, and $d_j^{i+1}d_j^i=1\otimes(d_P^{i+1}d_P^i)=0$, so these are cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $s\otimes p$, both $d_n^i\alpha^i$ and $\alpha^{i+1}d_{n-1}^i$ give $a(s)\otimes d_P^i(p)$; both $d_1^i\beta^i$ and $\beta^{i+1}d_n^i$ give $b(s)\otimes d_P^i(p)$. Equality on pure tensors gives equality of the sectionwise tensor maps and hence of their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Thus $\alpha,\beta$ are the claimed $R_n$-linear cochain maps.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), applied to the cochain differential and its naturality squares.

proof.text: For each $i$, flatness of $P^i$ means exactly that the sheaf tensor functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_B P^i$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Apply this defining property to the short exact $B$-module sequence of Step 5. The resulting short exact sequence is the restriction to $B$ of $\alpha^i,\beta^i$ constructed in Step 7. By Step 6 it is short exact also over $R_n$. This proves degreewise short exactness of the cochain sequence. Every argument was either sheafification, a calculation in a single degree, or the exact-functor definition of flatness; no points, sectionwise flatness, K-flatness, or degree bounds were used.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3): exactness of tensoring in the category of sheaf modules.
